headline: The Dinner & Special Meals Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet restaurant staff, book a table, order food and wine, ask simple questions, make polite requests and ask for help in Spanish, and start Dinner & Special Meals Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Say the Spanish sounds of table words clearly and greet a host or server politely.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent in dinner words; evening greetings

words.note: Spanish vowels are short and pure: a as in 'father', e as in 'met'.
In Latin America, c before e or i sounds like s: SEH-nah.
ch sounds like English 'church': koo-CHAH-rah.
j is a breathy h sound from the throat: AH-ho.
ll sounds like English y in most regions: ser-vee-YEH-tah.
rr is a strong rolled r; tap the tongue several times.
The written accent marks the stressed syllable: meh-NOO.
In Mexico, limón usually means a lime. Stress the last syllable.
Feminine noun, but it takes el in the singular: el agua fría.
Buenas noches works as hello and goodbye after dark. Cómo está is formal.

words.en: Nice to meet you, my name is Sam.

lessons.speaking: Greet the host with buenas noches, say your name, ask how they are, and say three table words clearly.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Give the size of your group, a dinner time and simple quantities of wine, food and pesos.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time with a las, and dinner quantities: glasses, bottles, kilos, pesos

words.note: Mexico says reservación; Spain says reserva.
Ask the time with ¿Qué hora es? Answer with Son las 8.

words.en: the wine glass, the glass of wine

words.note: In Mexico, una orden is one serving: una orden de tacos.
Fish is often priced by the kilo; ask the weight before you order.
Somos (we are) is the usual way to give your group size.

words.en: My reservation is at half past 8.
words.es: Mi reservación es a las 8 y media.
2 copas de vino tinto, por favor.
La botella de 600 pesos, por favor.

lessons.speaking: Tell the host how many people are in your group, what time your reservation is, and order 2 glasses of wine.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Describe dishes, tables and yourself with ser and estar at dinner.
lessons.focus: ser for what a dish or person is, estar for how food tastes now or where a table is

words.note: Changes to deliciosa for feminine nouns: la sopa está deliciosa.
Use picante for chili heat and caliente for temperature.
A woman server is la mesera.
estar: a condition that can change.

words.es: ¿Está libre la mesa de la terraza?

words.note: ser: what something is.
estar delicioso describes how this dish tastes right now.
ser: a normal feature of the dish.

words.en: I'm from Canada and I'm on vacation.
words.es: Soy de Canadá y estoy de vacaciones.

lessons.speaking: Tell the server where you are from, then say whether your dish is hot, cold, salty or delicious.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what you have, need and want at the table and ask if there is a table or a wait.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive for tables, wine and courses

words.note: Red wine is tinto, not rojo.

words.en: We have a reservation under Smith.
words.es: Tenemos una reservación a nombre de Smith.

words.en: I want the house red wine.
words.es: Quiero el vino tinto de la casa.
words.note: Quisiera (I'd like) sounds softer and more polite than quiero.

words.en: Do we have to wait long?
words.note: hay que + infinitive: it is necessary to.

words.en: We want a starter to share.

lessons.speaking: Ask the host if there is a table for your group, say you have a reservation, and ask if you have to wait.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going, what you plan to do and ask what you can do at dinner.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer and poder in dinner plans

words.note: A woman chef is la chef.

words.en: the after-dinner chat at the table
words.note: Lingering to talk after the meal is normal; no one rushes you.

words.en: I'm going to wait at the bar.
words.es: Voy a esperar en el bar.

words.en: We're going to celebrate our anniversary.
Can you make the fish without garlic?
I'm going to call the server.
words.note: Use the personal a before a person: al mesero, a la mesera.

lessons.speaking: Tell the host you are going to wait at the bar and that you are going to celebrate something, then ask if you can make a toast.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Say what you and others eat, drink and share using present-tense verbs.
lessons.focus: Regular present endings for -ar, -er, -ir verbs: tomo, comes, compartimos, cenan

words.note: pescado is fish on the plate; pez is a live fish.
In Mexico, an aperitivo is a drink before dinner; small snacks are botanas.
tomar is the everyday verb for drinking at a meal.
tú is informal, for a friend at your table.
llevar here means to contain: what does it have in it.

words.es: ¿Usted prepara el pescado a la parrilla?
words.note: usted is formal, for the server or chef.

words.en: People have dinner very late here.

lessons.speaking: Tell a dining companion what you eat and drink, ask what they eat, and say what you are sharing.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask the server what, which, how, where and how much about dishes, wine and the restaurant.
lessons.focus: Question words qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál with rising questions

words.note: Agrees with the noun: ¿cuántas personas?, ¿cuántos platos?
Two words with an accent for why; porque, one word, means because.
Use ¿cuál es...? to ask which one: ¿Cuál es el más popular?
Mexico often says platillo for a prepared dish.
Formal usted, for the server or sommelier.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el platillo típico de aquí?

lessons.speaking: Ask the server what they recommend, how a dish is prepared, and how much a bottle of wine costs.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say not yet, nothing more, another one, more or less while ordering and finishing dinner.
lessons.focus: no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no, más, menos and otro at the table

words.note: Spanish uses a double negative: No quiero nada.
Never put un before otro: otra copa, not una otra copa.
Say this when the server asks if you are ready to order.

words.en: We don't want anything else, thanks.
Another glass of white wine, please.
words.es: Otra copa de vino blanco, por favor.

lessons.speaking: Tell the server you are not ready yet, then ask for another drink and say you want nothing more after dessert.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Ask the server politely for the check, a photo and items at the table.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede…? and ¿Me puede…? requests and usted commands: traiga, espere, pase

words.note: vaso is a regular glass; copa is a glass with a stem.
Feminine because it is short for la fotografía.

words.en: Could you bring us the check, please?
words.es: ¿Nos puede traer la cuenta, por favor?

words.en: Could you take a photo of us?
Bring me a glass of water, please.
words.es: Tráigame un vaso de agua, por favor.
words.note: Usted command; por favor keeps it polite.

words.en: Excuse me, could you pass me the salt?

lessons.speaking: Ask the server politely for a glass of water and the check, and ask if you can pay by card.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Spot dinner cognates and use survival phrases to get help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad and -ente, and survival phrases for help

words.note: -ción words are feminine and match English -tion.
-dad words are feminine and match English -ty.
Many -ente words match English -ent.

words.en: I don't understand, can you speak more slowly?
How do you say this in Spanish?

words.note: Mexico says cacahuates. Say it before ordering and ask the server to check with the kitchen.

lessons.speaking: Tell the server you don't understand, ask them to repeat more slowly, and ask how to say a dish in Spanish.
